newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate down 90 bps to 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate down 90 bps to 11.3 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate slipped to 11.3 percent from 12.2 on Tuesday, amid high demand for pre-Christmas kuna funds, dealers said.
They put the total daily trade at 45 million kuna, of which 38.2 million were fresh borrowings. The rest was insurers' money, which they rolled over at a steady 9 percent.
Dealers said some borrowers were left empty-handed ahead of Christmas as their demand for further 25 million kuna could not be met.
Most new loans were call money at 11 percent, unchanged from Monday. One-week loans were struck at 14 percent.

The Zagreb money market is closed until Friday, for which the Central Bank calculated kuna midrates at 5.5276 against the dollar and at 3.55561 against the German mark. --Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
